phase1_initial_proposals.technology_specification: Permanent magnet direct current (PMDC) MRI scanner with superconducting magnets and liquid helium cooling system.
phase1_initial_proposals.technology_reasoning: This specification highlights the PMDC MRI scanner with superconducting magnets, which represents a significant leap in performance and efficiency. The use of superconducting magnets enables high-field strength imaging capabilities required for detailed medical diagnostics, while the liquid helium cooling system maintains this conductivity at cryogenic temperatures. Both components are large, complex assemblies that operate independently yet crucially together to provide high-quality magnetic resonance imaging.

components.name: Control Cabinet

phase1_initial_proposals.technology_specification: A conventional MRI machine designed for clinical use with a 3 Tesla magnet and liquid helium-cooled superconducting coil, producing high-resolution images.

The superconducting design using liquid helium is chosen because it allows for higher magnetic field strengths with efficient cooling mechanisms.
